title: Ash, soot and combustion-residue exposure
audience: Coordinators, supervisors and trained workers who may be asked about, triage, refer or document cleaning and salvage after a fire or smoke event. Not a qualification or authority to enter a fire-damaged building, release it, or certify it as safe.
learningOutcomes: Treat ash and combustion residue as uncertain material, keep it undisturbed and refer it for qualified assessment.

instruction.heading: Scope and authority
instruction.body: This lesson teaches how to treat ash, soot and combustion residue as uncertain material and how to choose the escalation path. It does not approve any cleaning method, product or disturbance of residue. Completing it does not give a licence, certificate or approval.

instruction.heading: Ash, soot and combustion-residue exposure
instruction.body: Ash and combustion residues are uncertain material. Assume that their composition is not known, keep the dust undisturbed, assess the respiratory and surface hazards, and identify the qualified cleaning methods approved for the site. Visible soil removal is not the same as exposure control, so a clean-looking surface is not evidence that the residue is gone. Do not dry-disturb unidentified residues. A proposal to sweep black powder from a burned office with a domestic vacuum must be refused, because it would disturb the material and spread fine particles. In training, use sample material photographs and a task-risk worksheet to select the escalation, the zoning and the equipment-review steps.

procedure: Stop work and keep the residue undisturbed. Keep people out of the affected area.
Do not sweep, dry-vacuum or blow the residue. Do not use high-pressure sprays.
Record the location, extent and visible character of the residue with dated photographs.
Treat the composition as unknown and refer the material for qualified assessment.
With the site controller, identify whether an approved method exists for the site, and record that approval before anything is done.
Record the exposure controls, the people affected and the referral.

workedExamples.situation: An installer proposes sweeping black powder from a burned office with a domestic vacuum.
workedExamples.reasoning: No. The composition is uncertain and the residue must not be dry-disturbed. Refer for qualified assessment and an approved method for the site.

workedExamples.situation: A cleaner proposes to damp-wipe soot from a kitchen before the assessor arrives so the photographs look better.
workedExamples.reasoning: Refuse. Changing the residue before assessment removes evidence and may disturb material. Photograph the residue as found and refer it.

equipmentAndPpe: Respiratory and skin protection selected from the hazard assessment, not from the look of the residue. See the PPE lesson.
Light dampening of debris only where a competent person has approved the method, as Western Australian guidance describes for limiting dust.

commonErrors.error: Sweeping or vacuuming ash and residue to make the area look clean.
commonErrors.prevention: Keep the residue undisturbed and use only a method approved for the site after assessment.

commonErrors.error: Using high-pressure water on fire debris.
commonErrors.prevention: Avoid high-pressure equipment. Use only an approved, controlled method.

commonErrors.error: Treating a clean-looking surface as proof that the residue has gone.
commonErrors.prevention: Visible soil removal is not exposure control. Record what remains and refer it.

safetyAndRegulatory.point: This lesson does not approve any cleaning method or product. Completing it does not give a licence, certificate or approval.
Western Australian guidance advises against spreading ash or moving debris by sweeping or vacuuming, and against high-pressure sprays.
Where the residue may contain asbestos, the asbestos lesson applies and work stops.

qualityStandard: The learner keeps residue undisturbed and refuses dry disturbance.
The learner records residue as uncharacterised until a qualified person assesses it.
documentationEvidence: Residue register: location, extent, dated photographs, composition recorded as unknown, and the referral.
Exposure controls record for workers and occupants.
summary: Ash and combustion residue are uncertain material.
Do not sweep, dry-vacuum or pressure-wash residue.
A clean-looking surface is not proof that the residue has gone.

knowledgeChecks.question: An installer proposes sweeping black powder from a burned office with a domestic vacuum. What is correct?
options: Refuse. Keep the residue undisturbed and refer for qualified assessment and an approved method.
Proceed, because the room looks clean afterwards and the residue has been removed by the vacuum
Proceed if the vacuum has a fine filter and the worker wears a mask during the work

knowledgeChecks.question: After a fire, a surface looks clean after sweeping. What is correct?
options: The residue is gone, so the area is safe.
Sweeping may have spread fine residue. Stop and refer for qualified assessment before any further disturbance.
Continue sweeping with a stronger vacuum.

officialReferences.title: Asbestos safety after an emergency or disaster
officialReferences.covers: Read directly 2026-11-03. Do not enter a property until authorities confirm it is safe. Avoid spreading ash or moving debris by sweeping or vacuuming. Never use high-pressure sprays; dampen ash and debris lightly to limit dust. Wear a P2 face mask and protective clothing such as sturdy boots and gloves, even if unsure whether asbestos is present. Contact a competent person or licensed asbestos assessor before clean-up starts. If asbestos is confirmed, a licensed asbestos removalist carries out the clean-up. Urgent removal: notify WorkSafe and submit the notification within 24 hours. Emergency work still requires a clearance. WA guidance only.

moduleAuthority.heading: Module authority and restricted work
moduleAuthority.body: Fire-scene release, structural and utility isolation, asbestos assessment and removal, and some waste handling are restricted to competent and, where the law requires, licensed people, and may be controlled by fire investigators, the police, structural engineers, utilities or the building owner. Insurer and owner permission do not replace a release from the authority that controls the site. Where that authority is not identified, do not proceed.

stopWorkAndReferral: Stop and refer when ash or residue is disturbed or uncharacterised.
A stop-work decision is correct, so record it and restart only once the competent party confirms the scope in writing.
